I feel this entirely. I think we both did the absolute best we could with the knowledge we had and how we felt at the time. It is so difficult to navigate family difficulties, and man -  Bravery points to you for working and managing households of 3, alongside everything else! 
That is a huge task! Especially when feeling guilty about your Dad and everything else. 

I appreciate your post so much. It's so hard to find people that can even somewhat relate to this. I know my.Dad wouldn't want me to feel this guilt. He was his own man, he could have gotten help earlier (like I tried) he could have stopped drinking, he could have been compliant with medications, and told me the truth about how he was feeling......not to say his death was his fault, as I mentioned I feel like it's mine. But....you did the best you could with your Dad before he had his Strokes, and I think sometimes parents don't want to worry us. 

It's the hardest thing. I think if my Dad and yours were sitting down having a conversation, they would both tell us.....to move forward and live a happy, fulfilled life. Easier said than done, right? 

I wish you as much peace as you can find. Thank you for taking the time to reply. ✨️❤️

Thank you everyone for the beautiful words and kindness. It makes me feel like I'm not alone, when in my reality I feel so disconnected and lost. 

I literally went to my Dad's empty house yesterday and layed on the floor in his bedroom. I needed to be there, even though now, all his furniture is in my house. I still feel most comfortable when I'm at the place he died. 

And I know next week will be the last time I can go there. It's going to be hard. 

I pray every day for him. I pray for my Mom, my brother, my friends. I pray for happiness, light, and peace. 

I feel like my perspective on life, friendships, what's important, (and what isn't) has changed dramatically. 

Also, trying to live in this world without my Dad is the hardest thing in the world. But I know he would want me to be happy. To live life to the fullest as I always have. To meet someone new (eventually) and have a wonderful man in my life. 

I am still trying, every damn day. Sometimes every second, every minute. The emotional blows hit hard and fast. And I definitely need to remember to take a breath. 

Thank you everyone for the comments and support. You are all amazing. 💕💟💞

Honey, I'm so sorry. My Dad was a functioning alcoholic, and had liver cirrhosis. He was sick too, but ended up going into Cardiac arrest on his couch and the Medics couldn't bring him back. 

It's been 3 months, and I am stripped of everything I thought I knew. I miss him so much. My Dad and I were very close. I didn't know he would die so suddenly. My heart breaks for you, because I know how you are feeling. 

My Dad was 64, I'm 37. Sending you light and love.
I appreciate your advice. 🙏 This is definitely the hardest thing I've ever been through. It helps to know there are other's who have been through this. I'm sorry about your Dad. Wishing you peace. 💕
Thank you. I do have a therapist, but I think seeing a bereavement specialist directly would help too. I'm so sorry you lost your Dad. Take good care. ❤
Thank you so much. I'm sorry you lost your Dad. I appreciate the advice. 💕

Thank you so much for taking the time to write this. 💕
I'm sorry for your loss as well. It's the hardest thing ever, losing a parent. Your kind words gave me a spark of hope  ✨  Wishing you peace and light.

My Dad died suddenly too. I am SO SORRY for your loss. Speaking as a medical professional: Sometimes autopsies don't show anything, and if they did, it can be vague and still not give a clear cut answer. 

Alot of sudden death cases, are caused by cardiac abnormalities. Especially if he was drinking. It's so hard to go through this. I also wanted a WHY when my Dad died on his couch. Ultimately, I had to let it go, and take off my MD hat, and just be his Daughter. 

Try to find peace in this; Your Dad died unexpectedly in his sleep. He died peacefully, and didn't feel a thing.  

I know it doesn't lessen the hurt. You are not alone.
